fact_text: A multibagger is described as a business that can compound its value by roughly 25-30% a year over many years, which turns an investment into 10x to 100x.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Winning Stocks - Everything you need to know' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Return on invested capital measures what a business earns on each rupee put into it, including plant cost and working capital, and the presenter treats long-run ROIC as the main driver of share-price growth.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Winning Stocks - Everything you need to know' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The presenter's illustration: a bank with a 35% ROIC can compound far more than a 15% ROIC peer over 5-10 years, so it can deliver better overall returns even if it looks pricier on price-to-book.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Winning Stocks - Everything you need to know' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Lucky Cement reinvested cement-plant profits into new plants and other businesses over many years, which the presenter cites as an example of high-ROIC compounding.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Winning Stocks - Everything you need to know' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The presenter's illustration: a 1 million tonne cement plant with a fair value near PKR 5 billion can be worth far more over time when its ROIC is high, because its profits fund further plants.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Winning Stocks - Everything you need to know' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The presenter values a stock by forecasting profit two to three years ahead, applying an expected price-to-earnings multiple to get a future fair value, and comparing it with today's price to see if the stock looks undervalued.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Winning Stocks - Everything you need to know' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The presenter argues the market tends to correct a mispricing within two to three years, since neither bull nor bear phases usually last long, which makes that horizon a reasonable test of valuation.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Winning Stocks - Everything you need to know' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: For Indus Motors the presenter's valuation approach forecasts units sold and profit per vehicle two to three years out, then applies a multiple to estimate the future share price.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Winning Stocks - Everything you need to know' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The presenter says a company's long-run shareholder-return record across both good and bad periods, looked at over about 20 years, is a key check on management quality.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Winning Stocks - Everything you need to know' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The presenter splits long-run stock returns into three parts: earnings or volume growth, dividends, and inflation or expansion into new industries, and says the mix depends on the sector.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Winning Stocks - Everything you need to know' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Fertilizer companies expand little but pay dividends of about 12-15% a year, which the presenter treats as a return component that needs no volume growth.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Winning Stocks - Everything you need to know' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: With cement dividends small and bag-price inflation near 6-7% a year, a cement stock needs roughly 18% annual volume growth, about a doubling of capacity every four years, to reach a 25% annual return.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Winning Stocks - Everything you need to know' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: A bank paying about a 10% dividend would need the remaining 15-20% of a target return to come from deposit growth, so the presenter tests banks by their deposit expansion.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Winning Stocks - Everything you need to know' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Millat Tractors sells about the same number of tractors as before, but profit per tractor has risen sharply, which the presenter cites as multibagger growth without a volume expansion.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Winning Stocks - Everything you need to know' (YouTube transcript, undated)
